newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil outlines remaining CVRD sale - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil outlines remaining CVRD sale - report.

text.p: Brazil's government and the National Development Bank (BNDES) have decided how to sell off the remaining 20.28 percent stake in mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.

The public share offer will consist of 78.79 million ordinary shares, representing 31.52 percent of voting capital, and follows the sale of 45 percent of CVRD's voting stock in May, the newspaper reported.

Based on the value of ordinary shares on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) Monday, the sale could total more than two billion reais ($1.8 billion) although most analysts expect the price to rise above its nominal 25.40 reais value.
Even without a premium, the offer will represent the largest sale ever of Brazilian shares abroad, Gazeta said.

Of the shares, 80 percent will be offered to international investors through the issue of American Depositary Shares (ADRs), while the domestic market will receive 20 percent with priority given to retail.

Local banks Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, Banco Real and Unibanco will offer shares in their branches and investment funds, called "Vale Funds", will have priority when the shares are allocated, Gazeta said.

The price of the shares will be determined through a bookbuilding system under which all interested buyers will submit a stock price, forming the basis by which the government determines the stock offer price.
In the domestic tranche, Vale Funds will benefit from a 10 percent discount but will have to keep the shares in their portfolio for at least six months.
Individuals will receive a four percent discount with a minimum investment of 10,000 reais and an obligation to keep the shares for three months.

The share offer is due to be launched on September 29 at domestic level while road shows for foreign investors will begin on October 13. The price of shares is scheduled to be determined in the week of November 10.
Merrill Lynch and Co Inc will be lead manager and NM Rothschild & Sons has been selected as co-manager.
